changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $d,k$ be natural numbers with $1\le k\le d/2$. Let $m$ and $r$ be the
natural quotients determined by
$$mk\le d<(m+1)k,\qquad 4r\le k<4(r+1).$$
Thus $m\ge2$. Write $[m]=\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ and give $[m]^k$ the Hamming
distance $d_H(\omega,\omega')=\#\{j<k:\omega_j\ne\omega'_j\}$. There is a
set $\mathcal C\subseteq[m]^k$ such that distinct $\omega,\omega'\in\mathcal C$
satisfy $d_H(\omega,\omega')>r$ and
$$\log|\mathcal C|\ge \frac{k}{1024}\log\!\left(\frac{ed}{k}\right).$$
For each $\omega\in\mathcal C$, place one $1$ in each of the first $k$ disjoint
coordinate blocks of size $m$, at position $\omega_j$ in block $j$, and put
$0$ in all remaining coordinates of $\mathbb R^d$. The resulting vectors
$u^\omega\in\{0,1\}^d$ have exactly $k$ nonzero coordinates and satisfy
$$\|u^\omega-u^{\omega'}\|_2^2>k/2\qquad(\omega\ne\omega').$$

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on the same measurable space
([[def-probability-measure]]). Absolute continuity $P\ll Q$ has the convention
of [[def-absolutely-continuous-with-respect-to-a-positive-measure]]. If
$P\not\ll Q$, define $D(P\|Q)=+\infty$. If $P\ll Q$, assume AC
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as in [[def-likelihood-ratio-as-rn-derivative]] and
let $r=dP/dQ$ be a finite-valued nonnegative measurable representative of its
Radon–Nikodym class; such a representative exists by
[[lem-radon-nikodym-density-of-a-finite-positive-measure-has-a-nonnegative-representative]].
On $\{r=0\}$ set $\ell=0$, and on $\{r>0\}$ set $\ell=\log r$. This
function is measurable: for $a\ge0$, $\{\ell>a\}=\{r>\exp(a)\}$, and for
$a<0$, $\{\ell>a\}=\{r=0\}\cup\{r>\exp(a)\}$, by the inverse and
monotonicity properties of the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]). These are
measurable sets by [[def-extended-real-valued-measurable-function]]. Since
$P(\{r=0\})=\int_{\{r=0\}}r\,dQ=0$ by
[[thm-likelihood-ratio-change-of-measure]], the value chosen there does not
affect $\int\ell\,dP$. Define
$$D(P\|Q):=\int \ell\,dP,$$
where $\log$ is the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]).

The definition is independent of the representative: two representatives
agree $Q$-almost everywhere, hence $P$-almost everywhere. Put
$$\psi(0):=0,\qquad \psi(t):=t\log t\quad(t>0).$$
The function $\psi$ is continuous at zero: for $s\ge1$,
$$0\le \frac{\log s}{s}=\frac1s\int_1^s\frac{du}{u}\le\frac1s\int_1^s\frac{du}{\sqrt u}\le\frac2{\sqrt s}.$$
Thus $t\log t\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$; here $L=\log$ by
[[cor-integral-logarithm-agrees-with-natural-logarithm]] and
[[def-integral-logarithm]]. On $(0,\infty)$, $\psi$ is a product of continuous
functions by [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]] and
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], so $\psi$ is continuous on
$[0,\infty)$ and $\psi(r)$ is measurable by
[[def-extended-real-valued-measurable-function]]. Its signed integral is
defined by the positive and negative parts
([[def-positive-and-negative-parts-of-a-function]],
[[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]]).

For $0<t\le1$, the function $-t\log t$ has derivative $-\log t-1$ and
maximum $1/e$ at $t=1/e$: $e=\exp(1)>1$ by
[[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]] and
[[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]], $1/e=\exp(-1)$ by
[[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], and $\log(1/e)=-1$ by
[[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]] and the inverse definition. The mean value
theorem gives increase before and decrease after this point
([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-integral-logarithm-derivative-and-normalisation]],
[[cor-integral-logarithm-agrees-with-natural-logarithm]], [[cor-mean-value-theorem]]).
At $t=0$ the negative part is zero. Since $Q$ is a probability measure,
$$\int \psi(r)^-\,dQ\le\frac1e.$$
The change-of-measure identity of [[thm-likelihood-ratio-change-of-measure]],
applied to $\ell^-$ gives $\int\ell^-\,dP=\int\psi(r)^-\,dQ\le1/e$,
so $\int\ell\,dP$ is well-defined; applying it to both positive and negative
parts gives
$$D(P\|Q)=\int\ell\,dP=\int\psi(r)\,dQ=\int r\log r\,dQ,$$
with $0\log0:=0$ and a finite negative part. Therefore the extended integral
is well-defined without an $\infty-\infty$ ambiguity.

This convention is directional: the first argument must be absolutely
continuous with respect to the second for the integral formula to apply.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Let $M\ge2$ be an integer, let $P_1,\ldots,P_M$ be probability measures on
one measurable sample space, and let $J$ be uniform on $[M]=\{1,\ldots,M\}$.
Conditional on $J=j$, let the observation $X$ have law $P_j$. Define the
mixture law
$$\bar P:=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M P_j$$
and the **mutual information** of this finite experiment by
$$I(J;X):=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M D(P_j\|\bar P).$$
The set function $\bar P$ is a probability measure: for disjoint measurable
sets $(A_m)$, countable additivity of the $P_j$ gives
$$\bar P\!\left(\bigcup_m A_m\right)=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M\sum_mP_j(A_m).$$
The finite sum commutes with the increasing partial-sum limits of these
nonnegative series, so
$$\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M\sum_mP_j(A_m)=\sum_m\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^MP_j(A_m)=\sum_m\bar P(A_m),$$
so $\bar P$ is countably additive; also $\bar P(\varnothing)=0$ and
$\bar P(X)=1$. Here $D$ is the directional KL
divergence of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]], and logarithms are natural.
For every measurable $A$, $P_j(A)\le M\bar P(A)$, so $P_j\ll\bar P$. Let
$r_j=dP_j/d\bar P$ be a finite-valued nonnegative density representative
provided by [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. If
$\bar P(\{r_j>M\})>0$, then for some integer $q\ge1$ the set
$E_q:=\{r_j\ge M+1/q\}$ has positive $\bar P$-measure. The change-of-measure
identity [[thm-likelihood-ratio-change-of-measure]] would give
$$P_j(E_q)=\int_{E_q}r_j\,d\bar P\ge(M+1/q)\bar P(E_q)>M\bar P(E_q),$$
contradicting $P_j(E_q)\le M\bar P(E_q)$. Hence $r_j\le M$ almost everywhere.
The densities also satisfy $M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M r_j=1$ $\bar P$-almost
everywhere: for each measurable $A$,
$$\bar P(A)=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^MP_j(A)=\int_A\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^Mr_j\,d\bar P,$$
so $M^{-1}\sum_jr_j$ and the constant function $1$ are both densities of
$\bar P$ with respect to itself. They agree almost everywhere by
[[thm-radon-nikodym-density-exists-and-is-unique-up-to-almost-everywhere-equality]].
For $0\le t\le M$, the positive part of $t\log t$ is at most $M\log M$,
while its negative part is bounded by $1/e$ in
[[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. Thus every term in the finite sum is
well-defined and finite.

The uniform prior is part of this definition. A nonuniform prior requires its
own weights in the mixture and in the KL average.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume AC. For probability measures $P,Q$ on one measurable space, with
$$\|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}:=\sup_{A}|P(A)-Q(A)|,$$
the event-supremum convention without a factor $1/2$,
$$\|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}\le\sqrt{\frac12D(P\|Q)}.$$
If $P\not\ll Q$, the right side is $+\infty$ by the definition of KL
divergence.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume AC. Let $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n\ge1$. For each $i<n$, let
$(X_i,\mathcal A_i)$ be a measurable space and let $P_i,Q_i$ be probability
measures on it. On the finite product measurable space set
$$P=\bigotimes_{i<n}P_i,\qquad Q=\bigotimes_{i<n}Q_i.$$
With the KL convention of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]],
$$D(P\|Q)=\sum_{i<n}D(P_i\|Q_i),$$
where a sum with an infinite term is $+\infty$.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume AC and let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ and $\tau>0$. For the normal location
laws with common variance $\tau^2$,
$$D\bigl(N(a,\tau^2)\|N(b,\tau^2)\bigr)=\frac{(a-b)^2}{2\tau^2}.$$

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let an experiment have parameter set $\{0,1\}$, sample space $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$,
and laws $P_0,P_1$. Let the scalar targets satisfy $t_0<t_1$ and put
$\Delta=t_1-t_0>0$. An arbitrary randomized estimator is a probability
kernel $K$ from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathbb R$ with its Borel sigma-algebra, and
its loss at parameter $j$ is squared error $(a-t_j)^2$. For every such $K$,
$$\max_{j\in\{0,1\}} R_j(K)\ge \frac{\Delta^2}{8}\bigl(1-\|P_0-P_1\|_{\rm TV}\bigr),$$
where $\|P_0-P_1\|_{\rm TV}=\sup_{A\in\mathcal A}|P_0(A)-P_1(A)|$.
Consequently the minimax risk over all randomized estimators obeys the same
lower bound.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $d\ge1$, $a>0$, and consider the finite experiment indexed by
$\omega\in\{0,1\}^d$ with sample laws $P_\omega$. The target is
$t_\omega=a\omega\in\mathbb R^d$, the action is in $\mathbb R^d$, and loss
is squared Euclidean distance. For each coordinate $i$, let $\omega^{(i)}$
denote the vector with bit $i$ flipped, and set
$$v:=\max_{\omega\in\{0,1\}^d,\ 1\le i\le d} \|P_\omega-P_{\omega^{(i)}}\|_{\rm TV}.$$
For every randomized estimator kernel $K$,
$$\max_{\omega}R_\omega(K)\ge\frac{a^2d}{8}(1-v),$$
and the same lower bound holds for the minimax risk. The total variation
convention is $\|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}=\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|$.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $M\ge2$ be finite, let $P_1,\ldots,P_M$ be sample laws on one
measurable space, and let $t_1,\ldots,t_M$ lie in a metric space
$(\mathcal T,\rho)$ with its Borel sigma-algebra. Suppose
$\rho(t_j,t_l)\ge\Delta>0$ whenever $j\ne l$. Let $J$ be uniform on
$[M]=\{1,\ldots,M\}$, with conditional observation law $P_j$ given $J=j$.
For any probability reference law $Q$, define
$$K_Q:=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M D(P_j\|Q)\in[0,+\infty].$$
For every randomized estimator kernel from the observation to $\mathcal T$,
with squared metric loss $\rho(a,t_j)^2$, its uniform average risk and its
maximum risk are each at least
$$\frac{\Delta^2}{4} \left(1-\frac{K_Q+\log2}{\log M}\right).$$
The minimax risk over all randomized estimators obeys this bound as well.
When $K_Q=+\infty$, the displayed lower bound is interpreted as $-\infty$
and is vacuous. Logarithms are natural.

changes.heading: Example
changes.after:
Let $n\ge1$ and $\sigma>0$. Observe independent
$X_1,\ldots,X_n\sim N(\theta,\sigma^2)$, and estimate the scalar mean
$\theta$ under squared-error loss. Restrict the parameter set to
$$\theta_0=-\frac{\sigma}{4\sqrt n},\qquad \theta_1=\frac{\sigma}{4\sqrt n}.$$
The minimax risk over this two-point experiment is at least
$$\frac{3\sigma^2}{128n}.$$

changes.heading: Example
changes.after:
Let $d,n\ge1$, $\sigma>0$, and $1\le k\le d/2$ be integers. Observe
$Y\in\mathbb R^d$ with independent coordinates
$Y_j\sim N(\mu_j,\sigma^2/n)$, and estimate $\mu$ under squared Euclidean
loss over
$$\Theta_{k,d}=\{\mu\in\mathbb R^d:\#\{j:\mu_j\ne0\}\le k\}.$$
For a randomized kernel $K$ to $\mathbb R^d$, set
$$R_\mu(K)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\int_{\mathbb R^d} \|a-\mu\|_2^2K(y,da)P_\mu(dy),$$
and define the minimax value here as $\inf_K\sup_{\mu\in\Theta_{k,d}}R_\mu(K)$.
There is a universal lower bound
$$\inf_K\sup_{\mu\in\Theta_{k,d}}R_\mu(K) \ge\frac{\sigma^2}{200000n}\,k\log\!\left(\frac{ed}{k}\right),$$
where $K$ ranges over randomized estimators. The range $1\le k\le d/2$
uses the local packing lemma proved on the A page.

changes.heading: Example
changes.after:
Let $d,n\ge1$, $\sigma>0$, and observe
$Y\in\mathbb R^d$ with independent coordinates
$Y_i\sim N(\theta_i,\sigma^2/n)$. Estimate $\theta$ under squared Euclidean
loss over the dense hypercube $\Theta=\{0,\sigma/\sqrt n\}^d$. Then the
minimax risk satisfies
$$\inf_K\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}R_\theta(K) \ge\frac{\sigma^2d}{16n}.$$

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Let $n,d\in\mathbb N$ with $n,d\ge1$, and let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ be a fixed design
matrix, and write $V_X:=\{X\theta:\theta\in\mathbb R^d\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n$
for its column space. For an observed vector $y\in\mathbb R^n$, the **fixed-design
least-squares fitted vector** is

$$\widehat\mu_X(y):=P_{V_X}y,$$

where $P_{V_X}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $V_X$, as defined in
[[def-orthogonal-projection]]. It is uniquely defined even when $X$ is rank
deficient. The nearest-point characterization in
[[thm-orthogonal-projection-is-the-unique-nearest-point]] says that
$\widehat\mu_X(y)$ minimizes $\|y-v\|_2$ over $v\in V_X$. This item defines the
fitted vector; it does not select a coefficient representation $\widehat\theta$.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
For $d,m\in\mathbb N$ with $1\le m\le d$,

$$\binom{d}{m}\le\left(\frac{ed}{m}\right)^m.$$

Here $\binom{d}{m}$ is the number of $m$-element subsets of a $d$-element set,
$m!$ is the factorial, $e=\exp(1)$, and integer powers have the convention of
[[def-integer-power]].

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let $W\subseteq V$ be a
linear subspace, and let $P_W:V\to W$ be the orthogonal projection. Then $P_W$
is linear and satisfies $\|P_Wx\|\le \|x\|$ for every $x\in V$. In particular,
$P_W$ is continuous.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $n,N\ge1$ and let $P_1,\ldots,P_N$ be orthogonal projections in
$\mathbb R^n$ onto fixed finite-dimensional subspaces $V_1,\ldots,V_N$. Let
$c_1,\ldots,c_N\in\mathbb R$ be fixed. For $y\in\mathbb R^n$, define
$q_i(y):=n^{-1}\|y-P_i y\|_2^2+c_i$, choose the least index attaining
$\min_{1\le i\le N}q_i(y)$, and return its fitted vector $P_i y$. The resulting
map $\widehat m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n$ is Borel measurable. The index map
is Borel measurable when $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has its discrete sigma-algebra.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge1$, $\sigma\ge0$, and let
$\varepsilon\sim N_n(0,\sigma^2I_n)$ be a centered multivariate normal vector.
Then for every $u\in\mathbb R^n$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb R$,
$$\mathbb E\exp(\lambda\langle u,\varepsilon\rangle) =\exp\!\left(\frac{\sigma^2\lambda^2\|u\|_2^2}{2}\right).$$
In particular, $\varepsilon$ is sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2$ in the
linear-functional sense of [[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]].

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
**Input:** naturals $n,d\ge1$, a fixed design $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, a data
vector $y\in\mathbb R^n$, and a penalty $\tau^2\ge0$.

List all supports $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ in lexicographic order of their
length-$d$ indicator vectors, using $0<1$. For each $S$, let $V_S$ be the span
of the corresponding columns of $X$, compute $\widehat\mu_S=P_{V_S}y$, and
score

$$q_S:=n^{-1}\|y-\widehat\mu_S\|_2^2+\tau^2|S|.$$

Initialize the incumbent at the first support and scan the rest in order,
replacing it exactly when a strictly smaller score is found; on a tie retain the
earlier support. Return the selected support $\widehat S$ and fitted vector
$\widehat\mu_{\mathrm{BIC}}=\widehat\mu_{\widehat S}$. The candidate family is
finite by [[cor-cardinality-of-the-power-set]], and the fitted-vector selection
is Borel measurable by [[lem-finite-support-projection-selection-is-borel]].
This is an exhaustive combinatorial procedure, not an efficiency guarantee.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
**Input:** naturals $n,d\ge1$, a fixed design $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, a data
vector $y\in\mathbb R^n$, and a natural $s$ with $0\le s\le d$.

**Candidate supports:** list all subsets $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with
$|S|\le s$ in lexicographic order of their length-$d$ indicator vectors,
using $0<1$. This is a finite nonempty list because it contains $\varnothing$
and is contained in the finite power set of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$.

**Procedure:** for each candidate $S$, let $V_S$ be the span of the columns of
$X$ indexed by $S$ and compute $\widehat\mu_S=P_{V_S}y$. Compute its residual
score $q_S=\|y-\widehat\mu_S\|_2^2$. Initialize the incumbent at the first
candidate. Scan the remaining candidates in the stated order, replacing the
incumbent exactly when a strictly smaller score is found; retain the earlier
candidate on a tie. Return the selected support and its fitted vector
$\widehat\mu_s$.

Each $V_S$ is finite-dimensional, so the projections are defined by
[[def-fixed-design-projection-estimator]]. The fitted-vector selection is Borel
measurable by [[lem-finite-support-projection-selection-is-borel]]. The procedure
performs a finite exhaustive support search; no computational-efficiency claim is
made.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $n,d\ge1$, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ be fixed, and put
$V=\operatorname{col}(X)$ and $r=\dim V$. Let $P_V$ be the orthogonal
projection and let $\mu\in\mathbb R^n$ be fixed. Let
$\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_n)$ be a centered random vector
with square-integrable coordinates satisfying
$\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i\varepsilon_j]=\sigma^2\mathbf 1_{i=j}$ for
$\sigma^2\ge0$. For $Y=\mu+\varepsilon$ and
$\widehat\mu=\widehat\mu_X(Y)$ as in
[[def-fixed-design-projection-estimator]],

$$\mathbb E\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2^2=\|P_V\mu-\mu\|_2^2+r\sigma^2.$$

In particular, when $\mu\in V$, the expected squared fitted-value error is
exactly $r\sigma^2$. The moment assumptions hold for centered Gaussian noise
with covariance matrix $\sigma^2 I_n$; Gaussianity is not otherwise needed.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $n\ge1$, let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a fixed subspace of dimension
$r$, and let $\mu\in V$. Suppose $Y=\mu+\varepsilon$, where
$\varepsilon\in\mathbb R^n$ is centered sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2\ge0$
in the linear-functional sense of
[[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]]. Put $\widehat\mu=P_VY$. Then
$\widehat\mu-\mu=P_V\varepsilon$.
If $r=0$ or $\sigma^2=0$, this error is zero almost surely. If $r\ge1$ and
$\sigma^2>0$, for every $t>0$,

$$\mathbb P\bigl(\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2^2>t\bigr)\le 2\cdot6^r\exp\!\left(-\frac{t}{8\sigma^2}\right).$$

Consequently, for every $0<\delta<1$,

$$\mathbb P\!\left(\frac1n\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2^2\le\frac{8\sigma^2}{n}\left[r\log6+\log\!\left(\frac2\delta\right)\right]\right)\ge1-\delta,$$

and

$$\mathbb E\left[\frac1n\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2^2\right]\le\frac{8\sigma^2}{n}\left(r\log6+\log2+\frac{13}{10}\right).$$
For $r\ge1$, both bounds are at most
$C\sigma^2(r+\log(1/\delta))/n$ and $C\sigma^2r/n$, respectively, for a
universal constant $C$. In the fixed-design model $Y=X\theta^*+\varepsilon$
with $\mu=X\theta^*\in\operatorname{col}(X)$, this is the fitted vector of
[[def-fixed-design-projection-estimator]].

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $n,d\ge1$, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ be fixed, and let
$\theta^*\in\mathbb R^d$ have a nonempty support
$S^*:=\{j:\theta_j^*\ne0\}$ of size $s:=|S^*|\ge1$. Suppose
$Y=X\theta^*+\varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R^n$ is centered
sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2\ge0$ in the linear-functional sense of
[[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]]. Run
[[alg-bic-penalized-least-squares]] with

$$\tau^2=16\log(6)\frac{\sigma^2}{n}+32\frac{\sigma^2\log(ed)}{n}.$$

For every admissible input to [[alg-bic-penalized-least-squares]], its finite
scan terminates and returns a support minimizing
$n^{-1}\|y-P_{V_S}y\|_2^2+\tau^2|S|$ over all supports. Among tied minimizers,
it returns the earliest support in the prescribed order.

Moreover, there is a universal constant
$C_0:=64+64\log6+32\log4$ such that, for every $0<\delta<1$,

$$\mathbb P\!\left(\frac1n\|\widehat\mu_{\mathrm{BIC}}-X\theta^*\|_2^2 \le C_0\frac{\sigma^2[s\log(ed)+\log(1/\delta)]}{n}\right)\ge1-\delta.$$

Since $s\ge1$, this also gives
$C_0\sigma^2s\log(ed/\delta)/n$. The theorem makes no design-rank,
incoherence, or column-normalization assumption. It asserts no zero right-hand
side when $s=0$.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
For every admissible input to [[alg-constrained-l0-least-squares]], its finite
scan terminates and returns a support minimizing $\|y-P_{V_S}y\|_2^2$ over all
supports of size at most $s$. Among tied minimizers, it returns the earliest
support in the prescribed order.

Moreover, let $n,d$ be positive integers, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ be fixed, and
let $\theta^*\in\mathbb R^d$ have at most $s$ nonzero coordinates, where
$1\le s\le d/2$. Suppose $Y=X\theta^*+\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon$ is centered
sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2\ge0$ in the linear-functional sense of
[[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]]. Let $\widehat\mu_s$ be the fitted vector
returned by [[alg-constrained-l0-least-squares]]. For $0<\delta<1$, with
$C:=32(4+2\log6)$,

$$\mathbb E\left[\frac1n\|\widehat\mu_s-X\theta^*\|_2^2\right] \le C\frac{\sigma^2s\log(ed/s)}{n},$$

and

$$\mathbb P\!\left(\frac1n\|\widehat\mu_s-X\theta^*\|_2^2 \le C\frac{\sigma^2\left[s\log(ed/s)+\log(1/\delta)\right]}{n}\right) \ge1-\delta.$$
No design-rank, incoherence, or column-normalization condition is assumed. The
claim concerns fitted values; it gives no coefficient-error bound.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n,d\ge1$, $\sigma>0$, and let
$1\le s\le d/2$ be integers. Observe $Z\in\mathbb R^d$ with independent
coordinates $Z_j\sim N(\theta_j,\sigma^2/n)$ for a parameter
$$\Theta_{s,d}:=\{\theta\in\mathbb R^d: |\{j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}:\theta_j\ne0\}|\le s\}.$$
For every Borel estimator $T:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$,
$$\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{s,d}} \mathbb E_\theta\|T(Z)-\theta\|_2^2 \ge \frac{\sigma^2s\log(ed/s)}{200000n}.$$

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n=d\ge2$, let $1\le s\le n/2$, and take
the fixed design $X=\sqrt n\,I_n$. For
$$\Theta_s:=\{\theta\in\mathbb R^n: |\{j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:\theta_j\ne0\}|\le s\},$$
observe $Y=X\theta+\varepsilon$ with one common noise law
$\varepsilon\sim N_n(0,\sigma^2I_n)$, where $\sigma>0$. For Borel fitted-vector
estimators $T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n$, define
$$R^*_{n,s}:=\inf_{T\ \mathrm{Borel}}\ \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_s} \mathbb E_\theta\left[\frac1n\|T(Y)-X\theta\|_2^2\right].$$
Then for $C=32(4+2\log6)$,
$$\frac{\sigma^2s\log(en/s)}{200000n} \le R^*_{n,s} \le\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_s}\mathbb E_\theta\left[ \frac1n\|\widehat\mu_s(Y)-X\theta\|_2^2\right] \le C\frac{\sigma^2s\log(en/s)}n,$$
where $\widehat\mu_s$ is the constrained support-search fitted vector. Thus
this Gaussian orthogonal-sequence model has a matching minimax rate up to
universal constants. The sparse upper-bound theorem itself is choice-free; this corollary
assumes AC for its Gaussian law and Fano lower-bound suppliers.

changes.heading: Statement refuted
changes.after:
For every fixed-design matrix $X$, the map $\theta\mapsto X\theta$ is injective;
therefore the coefficient vector is determined by its fitted mean.

changes.heading: Example
changes.after:
Let $n=d=2$, $X=I_2$, $\theta^*=0$, and impose sparsity $s=1$. Assume the
centered noise vector is sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2>0$ and has covariance
$\sigma^2 I_2$. The constrained support search retains the coordinate with the
larger squared observation. Its expected fitted-value error per observation is
between $\sigma^2/2$ and $\sigma^2$, and the general theorem gives the upper
bound $C\sigma^2\log(2e)/2$.

changes.heading: Example
changes.after:
Take one fixed-design observation with $X=[1]$, true fitted mean $\mu=0$, and
training response $Y=\varepsilon$. Let $\varepsilon'$ be an independent fresh
response error with the same mean-zero, variance-$\sigma^2$ law, where
$\sigma^2>0$. Least squares fits the one-dimensional column space exactly: its
training residual is zero, its expected error for estimating the mean is
$\sigma^2$, and its expected squared error for predicting the fresh response is
$2\sigma^2$.

changes.before:
Let $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$ be measurable and suppose $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$
for every $x$. Then
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu.$$
changes.after:
Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. Let $f_n:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable for every $n\ge1$, with $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$, and suppose $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$ for every $x\in X$. Then
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

changes.before:
Let $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$ be measurable and suppose $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$
for every $x$. Then
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu.$$
changes.after:
Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. Let $f_n:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable for every $n\ge1$, with $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$, and suppose $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$ for every $x\in X$. Then
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as used by [[def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws]]. For integers $d,n\ge1$, a noise scale $\sigma\ge0$, and a parameter $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, the Gaussian sequence observation is
$$Y_j=\theta_j+\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt n}Z_j,\qquad 1\le j\le d,$$
where $Z_1,\ldots,Z_d$ are independent random variables with law $N(0,1)$. The parameter is $s$-sparse when $0\le s\le d$ is an integer and at most $s$ coordinates of $\theta$ are nonzero. This is an observation model; it does not itself assert a risk bound or an optimal estimator.

[F1] [[def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws]]: under AC, $N(0,1)$ is the probability law with density $(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}$.
[F2] [[def-independent-random-elements]]: independence means independence of the sigma-algebras generated by the random variables; no coordinate independence is inferred unless stated.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Let $n,d\ge1$ be integers, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ be deterministic, and let $\theta^\ast\in\mathbb R^d$. The fixed-design regression model is
$$Y=X\theta^\ast+\varepsilon,$$
where $Y,\varepsilon$ are random vectors in $\mathbb R^n$. For $\sigma^2\ge0$, the noise is centered sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2$ when
$$\mathbb E e^{\lambda\langle u,\varepsilon\rangle}\le e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2\|u\|_2^2/2}\qquad(u\in\mathbb R^n,\ \lambda\in\mathbb R),$$
using the vector convention of [[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]]. No independence among the coordinates of $\varepsilon$ is assumed. The parameter is $s$-sparse when $1\le s\le d$ and $|\{j:\theta^\ast_j\ne0\}|\le s$.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
For integers $n,d,s$ with $n\ge1$ and $1\le s\le d$, and a deterministic matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, write $G=X^{\mathsf T}X/n$. The design satisfies the incoherence condition at sparsity $s$ if
$$\max_{1\le j,k\le d}|G_{jk}-\mathbf 1_{\{j=k\}}|\le\frac1{14s}.$$
Here the maximum is entrywise, $\mathbf 1_{\{j=k\}}$ is $1$ when $j=k$ and $0$ otherwise, and no probabilistic assumption on $X$ is made. The constant $1/(14s)$ is the exact premise used in the local restricted-eigenvalue derivation; it is not a generic definition of design compatibility.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Let $n,d\ge1$, $1\le s\le d$, and $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$. For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$, let $v_S$ be the vector agreeing with $v\in\mathbb R^d$ on $S$ and equal to zero off $S$; write $\|v\|_1=\sum_j|v_j|$ and use the Euclidean norm $\|\cdot\|_2$ of [[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]. The cone associated to $S$ is
$$\mathcal C(S)=\{v\in\mathbb R^d:\|v_{S^c}\|_1\le3\|v_S\|_1\}.$$
The design satisfies the restricted eigenvalue condition with constant $\kappa^2>0$ at sparsity $s$ when
$$\frac{\|Xv\|_2^2}{n}\ge\kappa^2\|v_S\|_2^2$$
for every $S$ with $|S|\le s$ and every nonzero $v\in\mathcal C(S)$. The denominator is the norm of the supported component; this condition does not assert a lower bound for all vectors in $\mathbb R^d$.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
For $n,d\ge1$, a deterministic design $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, response $y\in\mathbb R^n$, and penalty $\tau>0$, define the Lasso objective
$$Q_y(\theta)=\frac1n\|y-X\theta\|_2^2+2\tau\|\theta\|_1.$$
Its minimizer set is $\mathcal M(y)=\operatorname{argmin}_{\theta\in\mathbb R^d}Q_y(\theta)$. The penalty is strictly positive; no full-rank condition on $X$ is imposed. The nonemptiness, compactness, and convexity of this set are proved separately; this page defines the objective and minimizer set but does not select one minimizer.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after: Fix integers $n,d\ge1$, a deterministic matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, a response $y\in\mathbb R^n$, and a penalty $\tau>0$. The minimizer set $\mathcal M(y)$ of [[def-lasso-estimator]] is nonempty, compact, and convex.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $Y=X\theta^\ast+\varepsilon$ be the fixed-design model of [[def-subgaussian-fixed-design-regression-model]], let $S=\{j:\theta^\ast_j\ne0\}$, and let $\hat\theta$ be any minimizer of the objective in [[def-lasso-estimator]] with $\tau>0$. Write $\Delta=\hat\theta-\theta^\ast$. If
$$\left\|X^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon/n\right\|_\infty\le\tau/2,$$
then
$$\frac{\|X\Delta\|_2^2}{n}+\tau\|\Delta_{S^c}\|_1\le3\tau\|\Delta_S\|_1.$$
In particular, $\|\Delta_{S^c}\|_1\le3\|\Delta_S\|_1$, so $\Delta\in\mathcal C(S)$ for the cone in [[def-restricted-eigenvalue-condition]].

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $n\ge1$, $1\le s\le d$, and let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ satisfy the incoherence condition of [[def-fixed-design-incoherence-condition]]. For every $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with $|S|\le s$ and every $v\in\mathcal C(S)$,
$$\frac{\|Xv\|_2^2}{n}\ge\frac12\|v_S\|_2^2.$$
Consequently the restricted eigenvalue condition of [[def-restricted-eigenvalue-condition]] holds with $\kappa^2=1/2$.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $Y=X\theta^\ast+\varepsilon$ be as in [[def-subgaussian-fixed-design-regression-model]], with $n\ge1$, $d\ge1$, noise proxy $\sigma^2\ge0$, and $X$ satisfying the incoherence condition of [[def-fixed-design-incoherence-condition]] at some $1\le s\le d$. For $\delta\in(0,1)$ define
$$\tau=4\sigma\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log(2d)}{n}}+\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\delta)}{n}}\right).$$
Then
$$P\!\left(\left\|X^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon/n\right\|_\infty\le\tau/2\right)\ge1-\delta.$$

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $n,d,s$ be integers with $n\ge2$, $d\ge1$, $1\le s\le d$, and let $\sigma>0$, $\delta\in(0,1)$. In the model $Y=X\theta^\ast+\varepsilon$ of [[def-subgaussian-fixed-design-regression-model]], suppose $|\{j:\theta_j^\ast\ne0\}|\le s$ and the deterministic design satisfies the incoherence condition of [[def-fixed-design-incoherence-condition]]. Define
$$\tau=4\sigma\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log(2d)}{n}}+\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\delta)}{n}}\right).$$
For every response realization the minimizer set in [[def-lasso-estimator]] is nonempty by [[lem-lasso-objective-has-minimizer]]. The measurable score event has probability at least $1-\delta$, and on that event every minimizer $\hat\theta$ in the set satisfies
$$\frac{\|X\hat\theta-X\theta^\ast\|_2^2}{n}\le576\,s\sigma^2\frac{\log(2d/\delta)}n, \qquad \|\hat\theta-\theta^\ast\|_1\le96\sqrt2\,s\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(2d/\delta)}n}.$$
In particular, the prediction and coefficient rates are respectively $O(s\sigma^2\log(2d/\delta)/n)$ and $O(s\sigma\sqrt{\log(2d/\delta)/n})$. The design premise is essential to this fast-rate conclusion.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Let $n,p\ge1$ be integers and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent identically distributed random vectors in $\mathbb R^p$ with finite second moments, mean $\mu=\mathbb E X_1$, and covariance matrix
$$\Sigma=\mathbb E[(X_1-\mu)(X_1-\mu)^{\mathsf T}].$$
The oracle-centered sample covariance and the sample-centered covariance are respectively
$$\widehat\Sigma_\mu=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-\mu)(X_i-\mu)^{\mathsf T},\qquad \widehat\Sigma^\ast=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-\bar X)(X_i-\bar X)^{\mathsf T},\quad \bar X=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nX_i.$$
For a matrix estimate $A$, squared operator loss is $\|A-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2$, with the operator norm of [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]]. This definition distinguishes the known-mean raw second moment from the estimator that removes an unknown mean.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Let $p\ge2$ be an integer, $0\le q<1$, $c_{n,p}\ge0$, and $\tau>0$. For a symmetric covariance matrix $\Sigma=(\sigma_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le p}$, write
$$|\sigma_{-j,j}|_{(1)}\ge\cdots\ge|\sigma_{-j,j}|_{(p-1)}$$
for the magnitudes of the off-diagonal entries in column $j$, arranged in nonincreasing order. Define
$$G_q(c_{n,p})=\left\{\Sigma:\max_{1\le j\le p}\max_{1\le k\le p-1} k|\sigma_{-j,j}|_{(k)}^q\le c_{n,p}\right\}\quad(0<q<1).$$
For $q=0$, define $G_0(c_{n,p})$ to be the symmetric covariance matrices with at most $c_{n,p}$ nonzero off-diagonal entries in each column. The corresponding law class $\mathcal P_q(\tau,c_{n,p})$ consists of iid laws of $X\in\mathbb R^p$ whose covariance lies in $G_q(c_{n,p})$ and which satisfy
$$P(|v^{\mathsf T}(X-\mathbb E X)|>t)\le e^{-t^2/(2\tau)}
$$
for every unit vector $v$ and every $t>0$. This is a clean sub-Gaussian model; it assumes neither coordinate independence nor robustness to contamination.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Let $\mathcal Q$ be a family of probability laws on a common measurable sample space $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal C)$, and let $\Sigma(Q)\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ be a specified matrix parameter for each $Q\in\mathcal Q$, with fixed $p\ge1$. Give $\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ its usual Euclidean topology and Borel sigma-algebra. An estimator is a measurable map $\widehat\Sigma:(\mathcal Z,\mathcal C)\to(\mathbb R^{p\times p},\mathcal B(\mathbb R^{p\times p}))$. Define its squared operator risk at $Q$ and the minimax risk over $\mathcal Q$ by
$$R_Q(\widehat\Sigma)=\mathbb E_Q\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma(Q)\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2,\qquad\mathfrak R(\mathcal Q)=\inf_{\widehat\Sigma}\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q}R_Q(\widehat\Sigma).$$

For a family $\mathcal P$ of one-observation laws on a common measurable space $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ and an integer $n\ge1$, the $n$-observation experiment observes $n$ independent observations, each with law $P$. Its sample space is $(\mathcal X^n,\mathcal A^{\otimes n})$ and its sample law is the finite product probability measure $P^{\otimes n}$; this is the joint law of the IID family in [[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]] and [[def-independent-random-elements]]. For estimators $\widehat\Sigma:(\mathcal X^n,\mathcal A^{\otimes n})\to(\mathbb R^{p\times p},\mathcal B(\mathbb R^{p\times p}))$, define
$$R_{n,P}(\widehat\Sigma)=\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2,\qquad\mathfrak R_n(\mathcal P)=\inf_{\widehat\Sigma}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}R_{n,P}(\widehat\Sigma).$$

An infinite expectation is allowed, so every measurable estimator has an extended nonnegative risk. Suprema of risks are taken in the ordered range $[0,\infty]$, with $\sup\varnothing:=0$, its least element. Thus when $\mathcal Q$ or $\mathcal P$ is empty the corresponding supremum is zero for every estimator, and its minimax risk is zero. The estimator class is nonempty because the constant zero matrix map is measurable. The operator norm is from [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
For $\tau>0$ and $z\in\mathbb R$, define the **soft-thresholding map**
$$S_\tau(z)=\begin{cases}z-\tau,&z>\tau,\\0,&-\tau\le z\le\tau,\\z+\tau,&z<-\tau.\end{cases}$$

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after: Let $U,V$ be centered real random variables, not necessarily independent, each sub-Gaussian with proxy $K^2>0$ as in [[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]]. Then $W=UV-\mathbb E[UV]$ is sub-exponential with parameters $(256K^4,16K^2)$ under the restricted-MGF convention of that definition.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $A\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ be symmetric and let $\mathcal N$ be a $1/4$-net of the Euclidean unit sphere in $\mathbb R^p$. Then
$$\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\max_{v\in\mathcal N}|v^{\mathsf T}Av|.$$
The operator norm is the finite-dimensional norm of [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $A\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ be symmetric, where $p\ge1$. Then
$$\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\max_{\|v\|_2=1}|v^{\mathsf T}Av|=\max_j|\lambda_j|,$$
where $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_p$ are the eigenvalues of $A$.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$ be iid centered random vectors in $\mathbb R^p$ with covariance $\Sigma$ and finite second moments. Suppose each $Z_i$ is sub-Gaussian with vector proxy $L=\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, as in [[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]]. For $\delta\in(0,1)$ put
$$r=\frac{p+\log(4/\delta)}{n}.$$
For both the known-mean estimator $\widehat\Sigma_0=n^{-1}\sum_i Z_iZ_i^{\mathsf T}$ and the sample-centered estimator $\widehat\Sigma^*=n^{-1}\sum_i(Z_i-\bar Z)(Z_i-\bar Z)^{\mathsf T}$, where $\bar Z=n^{-1}\sum_iZ_i$,
$$P\left(\|\widehat\Sigma_0-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C L(\sqrt r+r)\right)\ge1-\delta, \qquad P\left(\|\widehat\Sigma^*-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C L(\sqrt r+r)\right)\ge1-\delta$$
for a universal constant $C$ (the proof permits $C=176$). Since $p\ge1$, this is equivalent up to a universal factor to the displayed dense rate with $p+\log(1/\delta)$. If $L=0$, both estimators equal $\Sigma=0$ almost surely.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Input: observations $X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbb R^p$, with integers $n\ge1$, $p\ge2$, and a fixed threshold constant $\gamma_\tau>0$ determined by the directional sub-Gaussian tail parameter $\tau$.

Compute the sample-centered covariance $\widehat\Sigma^\ast$ from [[def-sample-covariance-and-operator-norm-loss]] and put $\lambda=\gamma_\tau\sqrt{\log(p)/n}$. Output the symmetric matrix $\widehat\Sigma$ defined by
$$\widehat\sigma_{jj}=\widehat\sigma^\ast_{jj},\qquad \widehat\sigma_{jk}=\widehat\sigma^\ast_{jk}\mathbf 1\{|\widehat\sigma^\ast_{jk}|\ge\lambda\}\quad(j\ne k).$$
The diagonal is unchanged; an off-diagonal entry at threshold equality is retained. This procedure is a definition and makes no risk or positive-semidefiniteness guarantee.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $\Sigma\in G_q(c_{n,p})$ from [[def-weak-lq-sparse-covariance-class]], let $\widehat\Sigma$ be the output of [[alg-entrywise-thresholded-sample-covariance]] with threshold $\lambda>0$, and suppose
$$\max_{1\le j,k\le p}|\widehat\sigma^\ast_{jk}-\sigma_{jk}|\le\lambda/2.$$
Then
$$\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C_q\left(c_{n,p}\lambda^{1-q}+\lambda\right),$$
where $C_q<\infty$ depends only on $q$; for $q=0$, the class means at most $c_{n,p}$ nonzero off-diagonal entries per column and one may take $C_0=2$.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $X$ be a centered real random variable and let $\tau>0$. If
$$\mathbb P(|X|>t)\le2e^{-t^2/(2\tau)}\qquad(t>0),$$
then $X$ is sub-Gaussian with proxy $64\tau$ in the MGF convention of [[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]]:
$$\mathbb E e^{\lambda X}\le e^{32\tau\lambda^2}\qquad(\lambda\in\mathbb R).$$

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $U,V$ be real random variables on one probability space, not necessarily independent, and suppose for some $\tau>0$ that
$$\mathbb P(|U|>t)\le e^{-t^2/(2\tau)},\qquad \mathbb P(|V|>t)\le e^{-t^2/(2\tau)}\quad(t>0).$$
Then $W=UV-\mathbb E[UV]$ is well-defined, centered, and sub-exponential with parameters $(1024\tau^2,16\tau)$ in the convention of [[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]].

changes.heading: Statement

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be iid ([[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]) from $\mathcal P_q(\tau,c_{n,p})$ of [[def-weak-lq-sparse-covariance-class]], with $p\ge2$, $n\ge1$, $0\le q<1$, $\tau>0$, and $\log p\le n$. Use [[alg-entrywise-thresholded-sample-covariance]] with threshold
$$\lambda=8192\tau\sqrt{\frac{\log p}{n}}.$$
Then for a finite constant $C_q$ depending only on $q$,
$$\mathbb P\!\left( \|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le C_q\left[ c_{n,p}\left(\tau\sqrt{\frac{\log p}{n}}\right)^{1-q} +\tau\sqrt{\frac{\log p}{n}} \right]\right)\ge1-p^{-2}.$$
This is a high-probability bound; it does not assert an expected-risk or minimax lower bound.

changes.heading: Example
changes.after:
Let $n\ge d\ge1$, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ satisfy $X^TX=nI_d$, and let $Y\in\mathbb R^n$ be any response. Set $Z=X^TY/n$ and use the penalty $\tau>0$ from [[def-lasso-estimator]]. The unique Lasso minimizer has coordinates $\widehat\theta_j=S_\tau(Z_j)$.

In particular, if $Z_0\in\mathbb R^d$ is an observation from the sparse Gaussian sequence model of [[def-gaussian-sequence-sparse-means-model]] and $Y=XZ_0$, then $Z=Z_0$, so the same formula applies coordinatewise to that sequence observation. The square case $n=d$, $X=\sqrt n I_d$, and $Y=\sqrt n Z_0$ is included.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.before: For IID data with law P and an integrable jointly measurable criterion mθ, an M-estimator is a data-measurable exact or oP(1)-approximate maximizer or minimizer of Pn mθ. The maximizing and minimizing forms convert by replacing mθ with −mθ; existence is not asserted.
changes.after:
Let $P$ be a probability measure on a measurable observation space $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$, and let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be IID with law $P$; IID means a common law and mutual independence of the whole family ([[def-probability-measure]], [[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]). Let $(\Theta,d)$ be a metric candidate space with its Borel sigma-algebra ([[def-metric-space]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For each $\theta\in\Theta$, let $m_\theta:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and assume $P|m_\theta|<\infty$. Define
$$P_nm_\theta=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n m_\theta(X_i),\qquad Pm_\theta=\int m_\theta\,dP.$$

A measurable estimator sequence $\hat\theta_n$ into the Borel target $\Theta$ is an **M-estimator** if it maximizes or minimizes $\theta\mapsto P_nm_\theta$; measurability is as in [[def-estimator-sequence-in-iid-experiments]]. It is an exact maximizer when $P_nm_{\hat\theta_n}=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}P_nm_\theta$, and an $o_P(1)$-approximate maximizer when the finite measurable gap $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}P_nm_\theta-P_nm_{\hat\theta_n}$ is $o_P(1)$. For minimization use the gap $P_nm_{\hat\theta_n}-\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}P_nm_\theta$. The notation $o_P(1)$ is that of [[def-op-and-little-op-stochastic-bounds]].

The maximizing and minimizing forms are both included; replacing $m_\theta$ by $-m_\theta$ converts one to the other. This definition does not assert that a maximizer exists, nor that the population criterion $Pm_\theta$ has a unique maximizer. Whenever a random candidate is substituted into the empirical or population criterion, assume that evaluation is measurable and finite.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.before: For IID data with law P and integrable finite-dimensional estimating functions ψθ, a Z-estimator is a measurable exact or oP(1)-approximate root of Ψn(θ)=Pnψθ. No score equation is inferred from a nonsmooth M-criterion.
changes.after:
Let $P$ be a probability measure on $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$, let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be IID with law $P$ ([[def-probability-measure]], [[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]), and let $(\Theta,d)$ be a metric candidate space with its Borel sigma-algebra ([[def-metric-space]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Fix a finite integer $q\ge1$ and a norm on $\mathbb R^q$. For each $\theta\in\Theta$, let $\psi_\theta:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^q$ be measurable with $P\|\psi_\theta\|<\infty$. Define
$$\Psi_n(\theta)=P_n\psi_\theta=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_\theta(X_i),\qquad \Psi(\theta)=P\psi_\theta.$$

A measurable estimator sequence $\hat\theta_n$ into the Borel target $\Theta$ is a **Z-estimator** if it is an exact or $o_P(1)$-approximate root: $\Psi_n(\hat\theta_n)=0$ for every $n$, or $\|\Psi_n(\hat\theta_n)\|=o_P(1)$. Measurability is as in [[def-estimator-sequence-in-iid-experiments]], and $o_P(1)$ has the convention of [[def-op-and-little-op-stochastic-bounds]]. Whenever a random candidate is substituted into an estimating equation, assume the evaluation is measurable.

Because $q\ge1$ is finite, [[thm-all-norms-on-rn-are-equivalent]] gives constants $c,C>0$ with $c\|v\|_2\le\|v\|\le C\|v\|_2$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^q$. Thus for every $\mathbb R^q$-valued sequence, convergence of the chosen-norm tails to zero is equivalent to the Euclidean $o_P(1)$ convention in [[def-op-and-little-op-stochastic-bounds]].

This definition does not infer a Z-estimating equation from an M-criterion. Differentiating an M-criterion is justified only under additional differentiability and interior-point hypotheses; a nonsmooth criterion need not have a score equation.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.before: Uniform convergence in probability of the empirical criterion, positive population separation outside every metric neighborhood of θ0, and an oP(1)-approximate empirical maximizer relative to θ0 imply consistency in probability. The minimizing result follows by sign reversal.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.before: Uniform convergence in probability of a finite-dimensional empirical estimating equation, a separated unique population root, and an oP(1) empirical root residual imply consistency in probability.

changes.heading: Example
changes.before: The negative squared-error sample criterion is uniquely maximized at the sample mean; under a finite second moment its population criterion is uniquely maximized at the mean.
changes.after: Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be IID with law $P$, where $P|X|<\infty$ and $PX^2<\infty$. Let $\Theta=\mathbb R$ with its usual metric and set $m_\theta(x)=-(x-\theta)^2$. For a finite observed sample $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, the empirical criterion $P_nm_\theta$ has the unique maximizer $\bar x_n=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i$. The population criterion $Pm_\theta$ has the unique maximizer $\mu=PX$. The map from a sample to $\bar x_n$ is measurable, so it is an exact M-estimator.

changes.heading: Example
changes.before: The negative absolute-error empirical criterion is uniquely maximized at the middle order statistic for odd n and exactly on the interval between the two middle order statistics for even n; an explicit middle-point selection is measurable.
changes.after:
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be an IID sample from a law $P$ on $\mathbb R$ with $P|X|<\infty$. For a realized sample $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, let $x_{(1)}\le\cdots\le x_{(n)}$ be the order statistics and maximize
$$P_nm_\theta=-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n|x_i-\theta|,\qquad \theta\in\mathbb R.$$
If $n=2k+1$, the unique maximizer is $x_{(k+1)}$. If $n=2k$, the full maximizing set is $[x_{(k)},x_{(k+1)}]$. Choosing the middle order statistic for odd $n$ and the midpoint of the two middle order statistics for even $n$ gives a measurable exact M-estimator.

changes.heading: Example
changes.before: For a Bernoulli criterion indexed by {0,1} with p>0, an exact empirical maximizer is consistent for the unique population maximizer; a direct fourth-moment and summability proof gives the Bernoulli strong law and the finite-class uniform law.
changes.after: Let $0<p\le1$ and let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be IID Bernoulli$(p)$. Write $\bar X_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$. Take $\Theta=\{0,1\}$ with distance $d(\theta,\eta)=|\theta-\eta|$, and set $m_0(x)=0$ and $m_1(x)=x$. Let $\hat\theta_n=1$ when $\bar X_n>0$ and $\hat\theta_n=0$ when $\bar X_n=0$. Then $\hat\theta_n$ is an exact M-estimator and is consistent for the unique population maximizer $\theta_0=1$. This finite criterion class has a uniform law; the proof below gives the Bernoulli strong law directly.

changes.heading: Statement refuted
changes.before: With a constant criterion on Θ={0,1}, the alternating exact empirical maximizer has zero uniform criterion error but is not consistent for the fixed population maximizer 0.
changes.after: Without a separated population maximizer, every exact empirical M-estimator is still consistent for any fixed population maximizer.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.before: For finite-dimensional random vectors with r_n→∞ and r_n(T_n−θ)⇒Z, a pointwise first-order expansion of g at θ gives r_n(g(T_n)−g(θ))⇒AZ. If A=0 and a second-order Peano expansion with continuous symmetric bilinear H holds, then r_n²(g(T_n)−g(θ))⇒H[Z,Z]/2.
changes.after:
Let $d,k\ge1$, let $r_n>0$ be deterministic with $r_n\to\infty$, and let $T_n$ be $\mathbb R^d$-valued random vectors with target $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$. Suppose $Z_n=r_n(T_n-\theta)\Rightarrow Z$ for an $\mathbb R^d$-valued random vector $Z$. All vector norms below are Euclidean.

If $g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^k$ is Borel and there is a linear map $A:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^k$ such that
$$g(\theta+h)-g(\theta)=Ah+\rho_1(h),\qquad \frac{\|\rho_1(h)\|}{\|h\|}\longrightarrow0\quad(h\to0,\ h\ne0),$$
then
$$r_n\{g(T_n)-g(\theta)\}\Rightarrow AZ.$$

If, in addition, $A=0$ and there is a continuous symmetric bilinear map $H:\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^k$ such that
$$g(\theta+h)-g(\theta)=\frac12H[h,h]+\rho_2(h),\qquad \frac{\|\rho_2(h)\|}{\|h\|^2}\longrightarrow0\quad(h\to0,\ h\ne0),$$
then
$$r_n^2\{g(T_n)-g(\theta)\}\Rightarrow \frac12H[Z,Z].$$
For scalar-valued $g$, $H$ is the usual Hessian bilinear form. The second-order premise is a pointwise Peano expansion; continuous second derivatives on a neighborhood are not required.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.before: For iid observations, an o_P(n^{-1/2}) estimating-equation root that is consistent, has a nonsingular derivative of Pψ_θ at θ₀, finite score covariance, and local stochastic equicontinuity satisfies √n(θ̂_n−θ₀)=−V^{-1}G_nψ_{θ₀}+o_P(1)⇒N_d(0,V^{-1}ΣV^{-T}); AC is assumed through the library multivariate iid CLT.
changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC), as required by the library's multivariate iid central limit theorem. Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ be a measurable space, let $\Theta\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open with its Borel sigma-algebra, and let $\theta_0\in\Theta$. Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be iid $\mathcal X$-valued observations with law $P$. Let $\psi:\Theta\times\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^d$ be jointly measurable and satisfy $P\|\psi_\theta\|<\infty$ for every $\theta\in\Theta$; write $\psi_\theta(x)=\psi(\theta,x)$. Let $\hat\theta_n:(\mathcal X^n,\mathcal A^{\otimes n})\to(\Theta,\mathcal B(\Theta))$ be a measurable estimator sequence as in [[def-estimator-sequence-in-iid-experiments]] and a Z-estimator as in [[def-z-estimator]], with the stronger root-rate condition below. Write
$$P\psi_\theta=\mathbb E[\psi_\theta(X_1)],\qquad P_n\psi_\theta=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_\theta(X_i),\qquad \mathbb G_n\psi_\theta=\sqrt n(P_n-P)\psi_\theta.$$
Assume the displayed random vectors and suprema below are measurable, and suppose:

1. $\|\hat\theta_n-\theta_0\|=o_P(1)$ and $\sqrt n\,\|P_n\psi_{\hat\theta_n}\|=o_P(1)$.
2. $P\psi_{\theta_0}=0$, $P\|\psi_{\theta_0}\|^2<\infty$, and $\Sigma=P[\psi_{\theta_0}\psi_{\theta_0}^{T}]$.
3. The mean map $\Psi(\theta)=P\psi_\theta$ has expansion $\Psi(\theta_0+h)=Vh+\rho(h)$ with $V$ nonsingular and $\|\rho(h)\|/\|h\|\to0$ as $h\to0$, $h\ne0$.
4. The local stochastic-equicontinuity condition holds: for every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\limsup_{n\to\infty}P^n\!\left(\sup_{\theta\in\Theta:\,\|\theta-\theta_0\|<\delta}\|\mathbb G_n(\psi_\theta-\psi_{\theta_0})\|>\varepsilon\right)=0.$$

Here $P^n$ denotes the product sampling law of $(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$.

Then
$$\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)=-V^{-1}\mathbb G_n\psi_{\theta_0}+o_P(1)\Rightarrow N_d(0,V^{-1}\Sigma V^{-T}).$$
This theorem assumes consistency and the local empirical-process condition; it asserts neither. The local equicontinuity condition is the direct process hypothesis used in the proof, and consistency alone does not replace it.

changes.heading: Example
changes.before: For a positive sequence T_n with √n(T_n−1)⇒Z and the logarithm near 1, the first-order delta method gives √n(log T_n−log 1)⇒Z.
changes.after:
Let $\Omega=\{-1,1\}$ with each point having probability $1/2$, let $Z(\omega)=\omega$, and set $T_n=\max\{1/2,\,1+Z/\sqrt n\}$. Define the Borel map $g(t)=\log t$ for $t>0$ and $g(t)=0$ for $t\le0$. Then
$$\sqrt n\{\log T_n-\log1\}\Rightarrow Z.$$
Thus the log transformation has first-order scale $\sqrt n$ and derivative $g'(1)=1$ in this example.

changes.heading: Example
changes.before: At θ=(1,2), the ratio map g(x,y)=x/y has derivative (u,v)↦u/2−v/4; for the stated finite vector limit Z, the transformed limit is Z₁/2−Z₂/4 with variance 5/16.
changes.after:
Give $\Omega=\{-1,1\}^2$ equal mass $1/4$ at each point, and let $Z=(Z_1,Z_2)$ be the coordinate vector. Put $\theta=(1,2)$, $T_n=\theta+n^{-1/2}Z$, and define $g(x,y)=x/y$ for $y\ne0$ and $g(x,0)=0$. The denominator of $g(T_n)$ is positive for every $n$. The first-order delta method gives
$$\sqrt n\left(\frac{T_{n,1}}{T_{n,2}}-\frac12\right)\Rightarrow \frac12Z_1-\frac14Z_2.$$
The limit takes the values $1/4,3/4,-3/4,-1/4$ with equal probability and has variance $5/16$.

changes.heading: Example
changes.before: For g(t)=t² at θ=0 and T_n=Z/√n under the stated three-point law, the second-order delta method gives nT_n²⇒Z², with masses 1/2 at 0 and 2.
changes.after: Let $\Omega=\{-\sqrt2,0,\sqrt2\}$ with probabilities $1/4,1/2,1/4$, let $Z(\omega)=\omega$, and set $T_n=Z/\sqrt n$. For $g(t)=t^2$ at $\theta=0$, the first derivative vanishes and the second derivative is $2$. The second-order delta method gives $nT_n^2\Rightarrow Z^2$, which equals $0$ or $2$ with probability $1/2$ each.

changes.heading: Example
changes.before: For iid real X with a finite fourth absolute moment, the sample variance S_n²=Q_n−\bar X_n² has a Gaussian root-n limit with variance E[(X−μ₁)^4]−σ^4=μ₄−4μ₁μ₃+8μ₁²μ₂−4μ₁^4−μ₂²; AC is assumed through the multivariate iid CLT.
changes.after:
Assume AC. Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be iid real random variables with $\mathbb E|X_1|^4<\infty$. Put $\mu_j=\mathbb E[X_1^j]$ for $1\le j\le4$, $\sigma^2=\mu_2-\mu_1^2$, $\bar X_n=n^{-1}\sum_iX_i$, $Q_n=n^{-1}\sum_iX_i^2$, and $S_n^2=Q_n-\bar X_n^2$. Then
$$\sqrt n(S_n^2-\sigma^2)\Rightarrow N_1(0,\tau^2),\qquad \tau^2=\operatorname{Var}((X_1-\mu_1)^2)=\mathbb E[(X_1-\mu_1)^4]-\sigma^4=\mu_4-4\mu_1\mu_3+8\mu_1^2\mu_2-4\mu_1^4-\mu_2^2.$$
Here $\sigma^4=(\sigma^2)^2$ and $\tau^2=\operatorname{Var}((X_1-\mu_1)^2)$.

changes.heading: Statement refuted
changes.before: The claim that continuity at θ alone yields a first-order linear delta limit is false: for g(t)=|t| at zero and a symmetric two-point Z, √n|Z/√n| is the constant 1, not a linear image of Z.
changes.after: Continuity of $g$ at $\theta$ alone suffices for a first-order delta-method conclusion: whenever $r_n(T_n-\theta)\Rightarrow Z$, there is a linear map $A$ for which $r_n\{g(T_n)-g(\theta)\}\Rightarrow AZ$.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Let $\mathsf P:\Theta\to\mathcal P(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ be a parametric
model, let $\Theta$ be open in $\mathbb R^d$, and let a supplied sigma-finite
measure $\mu$ dominate every $P_\theta$
([[def-parametric-statistical-model]], [[def-dominated-statistical-experiment]]).
Supply as part of the setup a family of nonnegative finite-valued measurable
functions $p_\theta:\mathcal X\to[0,\infty)$ satisfying
$P_\theta(A)=\int_Ap_\theta\,d\mu$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$
([[def-measure-with-density]]). Thus each $p_\theta$ integrates to one.
The density family is supplied, rather than selected from domination alone;
no choice principle, joint measurability in $(\theta,x)$, or common
exceptional null set is asserted. A supplied extended-valued probability
density can be made finite-valued by setting it to zero on its measurable
infinite-value set, which has measure zero because its integral is one.
The QMD condition is unchanged by replacing any supplied density by an
almost-everywhere equal version: for each fixed $h$, the norm in the
condition below changes only on the union of two null sets.
At an interior point $\theta_0$, the model is
**quadratic-mean differentiable (QMD)** with score $s_{\theta_0}$ if
$s_{\theta_0}:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^d$ is measurable,
$\mathbb E_{\theta_0}\|s_{\theta_0}(X)\|^2<\infty$, and
$$
\int\left(\sqrt{p_{\theta_0+h}}-\sqrt{p_{\theta_0}}- \tfrac12 h^Ts_{\theta_0}\sqrt{p_{\theta_0}}\right)^2d\mu=o(\|h\|^2)
$$
as $h\to0$ with $\theta_0+h\in\Theta$. Values of the score on
$\{p_{\theta_0}=0\}$ do not affect this condition. The Fisher information
associated with this QMD score is
$I_{\theta_0}=\mathbb E_{\theta_0}[s_{\theta_0}s_{\theta_0}^T]$; it may be
singular. QMD is an $L^2(\mu)$ condition and does not assert pointwise
differentiability of $p_\theta$ or local mutual absolute continuity of
$P_\theta$ and $P_{\theta_0}$.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Let a dominated finite-dimensional parametric model be quadratic-mean
differentiable, with the supplied density family of [[def-qmd-path]], at an interior point $\theta_0\in\mathbb R^d$, with score
$s_{\theta_0}\in L^2(P_{\theta_0};\mathbb R^d)$. Then
$\mathbb E_{\theta_0}s_{\theta_0}=0$.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Assume AC for the supplied density representatives in
[[def-score-and-fisher-information]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Let
$X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be iid from a dominated parametric model on an open
$\Theta\subset\mathbb R^d$, and let $\ell_n(\theta)=\sum_{i=1}^n\log
p_\theta(X_i)$. For any nested null $\Theta_0\subseteq\Theta$ for which the
maxima exist, the **likelihood-ratio statistic** is
$$L_n=2\left\{\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\ell_n(\theta)-\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_0}\ell_n(\theta)\right\}.$$

For the Wald and score statistics, specialize to a **regular equality null of
codimension $q$** at an interior point $\theta_0$: this is a null set which,
in a $C^1$ local parameter chart
$\theta=(\psi,\eta)\in\mathbb R^q\times\mathbb R^{d-q}$, is $\psi=0$ near
$\theta_0=(0,\eta_0)$. Its local tangent is the $\eta$-coordinate subspace.
Assume the QMD information $I(\theta_0)$ is positive definite. Let
$\hat\theta_n$ maximize $\ell_n$ over the full parameter space $\Theta$ and
$\tilde\theta_n$ maximize it over the null $\Theta_0$, so the general
likelihood-ratio definition is
$L_n=2\{\ell_n(\hat\theta_n)-\ell_n(\tilde\theta_n)\}$.

For the score statistic, assume $\log p_\theta(x)$ is differentiable in the
local chart at the parameter values where it is evaluated, and write
$s_\theta(x)=\nabla_\theta\log p_\theta(x)$. Require explicitly that this
pointwise derivative at $\theta_0$ agrees $P_{\theta_0}$-almost surely with
the QMD score; this compatibility is an assumption, not a consequence of QMD
alone. The pointwise score and its information-matrix convention are those in
[[def-score-and-fisher-information]].

Partition the score and information in $(\psi,\eta)$ coordinates:
$s=(s_\psi,s_\eta)$ and
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}I_{\psi\psi}&I_{\psi\eta}\\I_{\eta\psi}&I_{\eta\eta}\end{pmatrix},\qquad I_{\mathrm{eff}}=I_{\psi\psi}-I_{\psi\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}I_{\eta\psi}.$$
The matrix $I_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the information for the tested coordinates
after accounting for the nuisance coordinates. If $d=q$, interpret empty-block
products as zero, so $I_{\mathrm{eff}}=I_{\psi\psi}=I$ and $C$ below is the
empty $q\times0$ matrix. If $d>q$, then $I_{\eta\eta}$ is positive definite;
for $z\ne0$, the quadratic form of $I$ at
$(z,-I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}I_{\eta\psi}z)$ equals
$z^TI_{\mathrm{eff}}z>0$. Thus $I_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is positive definite in
either case. Put
$$
U_n(\theta)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n s_\theta(X_i).
$$
For a consistent estimator $\widehat I_{\mathrm{eff},n}$ of
$I_{\mathrm{eff}}$ and a consistent estimator $\widehat C_n$ of
$C=I_{\psi\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}$, set
$U_{\mathrm{eff},n}=U_{\psi,n}(\tilde\theta_n)-
\widehat C_nU_{\eta,n}(\tilde\theta_n)$. The **score statistic** is
$S_n=U_{\mathrm{eff},n}^T\widehat I_{\mathrm{eff},n}^{-1}U_{\mathrm{eff},n}$.
For a consistent covariance estimator $\widehat V_{\psi,n}$ of the
$\psi$-block of $I^{-1}$, the **Wald statistic** is
$W_n=n\hat\psi_n^T\widehat V_{\psi,n}^{-1}\hat\psi_n$, where
$\hat\psi_n$ is the tested coordinate of $\hat\theta_n$. When a displayed
inverse does not exist, set that statistic to zero; under the regularity
conditions used in the later calibration theorem, the inverse exists with
probability tending to one. This definition gives the statistics and their
normalizations; it asserts no finite-sample or asymptotic distribution.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be iid with law
$P_{\theta_0}$ in a dominated parametric model
$\{P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}$, where $\Theta$ is open in $\mathbb R^d$,
$d\ge1$, and $\theta_0\in\Theta$. Let $p_\theta$ be densities with respect
to one supplied sigma-finite measure. Suppose the model is QMD at $\theta_0$
with score $s_{\theta_0}$ and positive-definite information
$I=\mathbb E_{\theta_0}[s_{\theta_0}s_{\theta_0}^T]$. Assume there are a
neighborhood $V$ of $\theta_0$ and a nonnegative measurable $L$ with
$\mathbb E_{\theta_0}L^2<\infty$ such that, on one $P_{\theta_0}$-full set,
$$
|\log p_{\theta_1}(x)-\log p_{\theta_2}(x)|\le L(x)\|\theta_1-\theta_2\| \qquad(\theta_1,\theta_2\in V).
$$
Suppose a measurable exact MLE $\hat\theta_n$ exists and is consistent, in
the sense that $P_{\theta_0}(\|\hat\theta_n-\theta_0\|>\varepsilon)\to0$
for every $\varepsilon>0$. Then
$$\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)=I^{-1}\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n s_{\theta_0}(X_i)+o_{P_{\theta_0}}(1)\ \Rightarrow\ N_d(0,I^{-1}).$$
Under the same local hypotheses, every consistent measurable exact likelihood
maximizer over a possibly $n$-dependent subset that contains $\theta_0$ is
also root-$n$ bounded in probability.
The conclusion is asymptotic; it gives no exact finite-sample normal law.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be iid from $P_{\theta_0}$ in a correctly
specified dominated model, with $\theta_0=(0,\eta_0)$ an interior point of
the full open parameter set $\Theta\subset\mathbb R^q\times\mathbb R^{d-q}$.
In a local $C^1$ parameter chart, suppose the null is $\psi=0$, so its local
null set is a linear subspace of codimension $q\ge1$; all score and
information coordinates below use this chart. Assume QMD at
$\theta_0$ with positive-definite information
$$
I=\begin{pmatrix}I_{\psi\psi}&I_{\psi\eta}\\I_{\eta\psi}&I_{\eta\eta}\end{pmatrix},
$$
and write $I_{\mathrm{eff}}=I_{\psi\psi}-
I_{\psi\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}I_{\eta\psi}$. If $d=q$, interpret nuisance
blocks as empty, so $I_{\mathrm{eff}}=I_{\psi\psi}=I$ and products involving
$\eta$ are zero. Let
$\Delta_n=n^{-1/2}\sum_i s_{\theta_0}(X_i)$. Assume the hypotheses of
[[thm-regular-mle-asymptotic-linearity-and-normality]] hold for the full model.
Assume the constrained MLE is measurable, exact, consistent, and maximizes
over a set containing $\theta_0$; it is root-$n$ bounded by that theorem's
localization conclusion. For every finite $M$ the
following likelihood and score expansions hold uniformly over $\|h\|\le M$:
$$
\ell_n(\theta_0+h/\sqrt n)-\ell_n(\theta_0) =h^T\Delta_n-\tfrac12h^TIh+o_P(1),
$$
$$
n^{-1/2}\nabla\ell_n(\theta_0+h/\sqrt n) =\Delta_n-Ih+o_P(1).
$$
Assume the covariance, score-projection, and efficient-information estimators in
[[def-wald-score-likelihood-ratio-statistics]] converge in probability to
their stated limits. Partition $\Delta_n=(\Delta_{\psi,n},\Delta_{\eta,n})$,
put $r_n=\Delta_{\psi,n}-I_{\psi\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}\Delta_{\eta,n}$,
and set $T_n=r_n^TI_{\mathrm{eff}}^{-1}r_n$. Then, under the null,
$$
W_n=T_n+o_P(1),\quad S_n=T_n+o_P(1),\quad L_n=T_n+o_P(1),\qquad W_n\Rightarrow\chi_q^2,\quad S_n\Rightarrow\chi_q^2,\quad L_n\Rightarrow\chi_q^2.
$$
Here $\chi_q^2$ is the law defined in [[def-chi-square-law]]. This is an
asymptotic calibration; no exact finite-sample
chi-square law is asserted.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume AC and the hypotheses of
[[thm-wald-score-likelihood-ratio-asymptotic-chi-square]]. Under the null,
the three statistics satisfy
$W_n-S_n=o_P(1)$, $S_n-L_n=o_P(1)$, and $L_n-W_n=o_P(1)$. Hence they have
the same first-order null calibration, namely $\chi_q^2$.

changes.heading: Example
changes.after:
Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be iid $N(\mu,\sigma^2)$ with known
$\sigma>0$, and test $H_0:\mu=\mu_0$ in the one-dimensional location model.
The sample mean is the unique MLE. In this model, the Wald, score, and
likelihood-ratio statistics are exactly equal to
$n(\bar X-\mu_0)^2/\sigma^2$, which has the exact $\chi_1^2$ law under $H_0$.
The notation $\chi_1^2$ is as in [[def-chi-square-law]]. This is a
special finite-sample identity and does not make the general calibration
theorem exact.

changes.heading: Statement refuted
changes.after:
For the one-sided null $H_0:\mu\le0$ in a smooth normal location model, the
likelihood-ratio statistic has a $\chi_1^2$ limit at $\mu=0$ merely because
$\mu=0$ is interior to the full parameter space.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ be one measurable space and let $P_n,Q_n$ be
probability measures on it ([[def-probability-measure]]). The sequence
$(Q_n)$ is **contiguous with respect to** $(P_n)$, written $Q_n\triangleleft
P_n$, if for every sequence $A_n\in\mathcal A$,
$$P_n(A_n)\longrightarrow0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Q_n(A_n)\longrightarrow0.$$
The sequences are **mutually contiguous**, written $Q_n\triangleleft\triangleright
P_n$, if both $Q_n\triangleleft P_n$ and $P_n\triangleleft Q_n$.

Contiguity is a relation between sequences of laws, not absolute continuity at
each finite $n$. It says that events negligible under one sequence remain
negligible under the other in the indicated direction.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume countable choice. For every convex set $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, its
topological boundary $\partial C=\overline C\setminus C^\circ$ has
$d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero. If $C$ has empty interior, then $C$
itself is contained in a proper affine subspace and is Lebesgue null.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Let $P_{n,h}$ be probability laws on a common measurable space for each
integer $n\ge1$ and local parameter $h\in\mathbb R^d$, where $d<\infty$ and
$P_{n,0}$ is the base law. Suppose that for every fixed $h$ we are supplied a
nonnegative measurable function $L_{n,h}$ with
$$\int L_{n,h}\,dP_{n,0}=1.$$
It defines an absolutely continuous proxy
$$\bar P_{n,h}(A):=\int_A L_{n,h}\,dP_{n,0}.$$
The actual local law is allowed to have a singular part; the approximation
condition below is what connects it to this proxy.

The experiments are **locally asymptotically normal (LAN)** at $h=0$ with
information matrix $K$ and central sequence $\Delta_n$ if $K$ is a symmetric
positive semidefinite $d\times d$ matrix, $\Delta_n$ is an $\mathbb R^d$-valued
statistic,
$$\Delta_n\Rightarrow N_d(0,K)\quad\text{under }P_{n,0},$$
and for every fixed $h\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$\|P_{n,h}-\bar P_{n,h}\|_{\rm TV}\to0,\qquad \log L_{n,h}=h^T\Delta_n-\tfrac12h^TKh+o_{P_{n,0}}(1),$$
where $\|\cdot\|_{\rm TV}$ is the event-supremum total variation distance
([[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]]) and
$o_{P_{n,0}}(1)$ means convergence to zero in $P_{n,0}$-probability. We set
$\log0=-\infty$; the finite-valued expansion entails
$P_{n,0}(L_{n,h}=0)\to0$. Convergence in distribution is as in
[[def-convergence-in-distribution-of-random-elements]], and $N_d(0,K)$ allows
singular $K$ ([[def-multivariate-normal-law]]).

If $P_{n,h}=\bar P_{n,h}$, this is the usual dominated LAN comparison. The
proxy formulation also covers QMD paths whose local alternatives are not
absolutely continuous with respect to the base law, provided the singular
product mass tends to zero in total variation. This definition is pointwise
in each fixed $h$; it does not assert uniformity over bounded sets of $h$.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume countable choice. Let $d\ge1$ and let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be
nonempty compact convex sets. With $A+B=\{a+b:a\in A,b\in B\}$ and
$\lambda_d$ denoting Lebesgue measure,
$$\lambda_d(A+B)^{1/d}\ge \lambda_d(A)^{1/d}+\lambda_d(B)^{1/d}.$$
Zero-volume and lower-dimensional sets are included.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
For each $n$, let $P_n,Q_n$ be probability measures on one measurable space,
and let $L_n\ge0$ satisfy $Q_n(A)=\int_A L_n\,dP_n$ for every measurable
$A$. Suppose $E_{P_n}L_n=1$, $L_n\Rightarrow L$ under $P_n$, $L\ge0$, and
$E L=1$. Then $(Q_n)$ is contiguous with respect to $(P_n)$.

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
In a local experiment $\{P_{n,h}:h\in\mathbb R^d\}$ at $h=0$
([[def-lan-experiment]]), let $T_n$ be an $\mathbb R^d$-valued statistic.
It is **regular at zero with limit law $W$** if, for every fixed
$h\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$T_n-h\Rightarrow W\quad\text{under }P_{n,h},$$
where the same probability law $W$ works for all $h$. In a parametric model
with true parameter $\theta_0$, this is the definition for
$T_n=\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_0)$ and local laws at
$\theta_0+h/\sqrt n$; equivalently the centered error
$\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_0-h/\sqrt n)$ has a limit independent of
the fixed local displacement $h$.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume AC.

Let $H\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact, let $\pi$ be a probability measure on
$H$, and let $P_{n,0}$ be base laws. Suppose $L_n(h,x)$ is jointly measurable
in $(h,x)$, nonnegative, and satisfies
$\int L_n(h,x)P_{n,0}(dx)=1$ for every $h\in H$. Let
$\Delta_n\Rightarrow Z\sim N_d(0,K)$ under $P_{n,0}$, where $K$ is positive
semidefinite, and put
$$g_h(z)=\exp(h^Tz-\tfrac12h^TKh).$$
Assume the random variable
$$a_n(x):=\sup_{h\in H}|L_n(h,x)-g_h(\Delta_n(x))|$$
is measurable and $E_{P_{n,0}}a_n\to0$. Let the prior-predictive law be
$M_n(dx)=m_n(x)P_{n,0}(dx)$ with
$m_n(x)=\int_HL_n(h,x)\pi(dh)$, and define posteriors
$$\Pi_n(dh\mid x)=\frac{L_n(h,x)\pi(dh)}{m_n(x)},\qquad \Pi^G(dh\mid z)=\frac{g_h(z)\pi(dh)}{m(z)},\quad m(z)=\int_Hg_h(z)\pi(dh),$$
where an arbitrary probability measure is assigned if a denominator is zero.
Then
$$E_{M_n}\int_H\left| \frac{L_n(h,X)}{m_n(X)}- \frac{g_h(\Delta_n(X))}{m(\Delta_n(X))} \right|\pi(dh)\longrightarrow0.$$
In particular the posterior laws converge in expected total variation,
because their event-probability differences are bounded by this $L^1(\pi)$
distance. The convention for total variation is
[[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]].

This lemma assumes an $L^1$ uniform likelihood-field approximation. Pointwise
LAN alone does not supply that hypothesis.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume AC. Let $X\sim N_d(m,\Sigma)$ with positive-definite covariance
$\Sigma$. Let $L:\mathbb R^d\to[0,M]$ be Borel measurable and symmetric,
$L(-x)=L(x)$, and quasi-convex, meaning each sublevel set
$\{x:L(x)\le t\}$ is convex. Then for every $a\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$E L(X-a)\ge E L(X-m).$$
Thus the Gaussian center $m$ minimizes expected loss. The result includes
quasi-convex losses whose sublevel sets are not closed.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume AC.

Let $P_n$ be probability measures and let $Q_n=L_nP_n$, where $L_n\ge0$ and
$E_{P_n}L_n=1$. Let $T_n$ take values in $\mathbb R^k$. Suppose under $P_n$
that $(T_n,L_n)\Rightarrow(T,e^Z)$, where $Z$ is normal with mean
$-\sigma^2/2$ and variance $\sigma^2$; the joint law of $(T,Z)$ need not be
Gaussian. Then under $Q_n$, $T_n$ converges in distribution to the probability
law determined by
$$E[f(T^{(Q)})]=E[e^Zf(T)]$$
for every bounded continuous $f$. In particular, $Q_n$ is contiguous with
respect to $P_n$. If $(T,Z)$ is jointly Gaussian with
$T\sim N_k(\mu,\Sigma)$ and $\operatorname{Cov}(T,Z)=\tau$, this tilted
law is $N_k(\mu+\tau,\Sigma)$, including singular $\Sigma$.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.before:
Assume AC. Let $L:\mathbb R^d\to[0,M]$ be Borel measurable, symmetric and quasi-convex, with $M>0$. For integers $N\ge2$ and $m\ge1$, put $\delta=M/N$, $C_k=\overline{\{x:L(x)\le k\delta\}}$ and
$$g_{N,m}(x)=\delta\sum_{k=1}^{N-1}\min(1,m\,d(x,C_k)).$$
For $C_k=\varnothing$ the corresponding summand is defined to be one, and for $C_k=\mathbb R^d$ it is zero. Then $0\le g_{N,m}\le L$, and $g_{N,m}$ is bounded and Lipschitz. For every nondegenerate Gaussian $H\sim N_d(b,S)$,
$$\inf_a E g_{N,m}(a-H)=E g_{N,m}(H-b),\qquad
\lim_{N\to\infty}\lim_{m\to\infty}E g_{N,m}(H-b)=E L(H-b).$$
Each summand is symmetric and quasi-convex; no quasi-convexity of their sum is asserted.
changes.after:
Assume AC. Let $L:\mathbb R^d\to[0,M]$ be Borel measurable, symmetric and quasi-convex, with $M>0$. For integers $N\ge2$ and $m\ge1$, put $\delta=M/N$, $C_k=\overline{\{x:L(x)\le k\delta\}}$ and
$$g_{N,m}(x)=\delta\sum_{k=1}^{N-1}\min(1,m\,d(x,C_k)).$$
For $C_k=\varnothing$ the corresponding summand is defined to be one, and for $C_k=\mathbb R^d$ it is zero. Then $0\le g_{N,m}\le L$, and $g_{N,m}$ is bounded and Lipschitz. For every nondegenerate Gaussian $H\sim N_d(b,S)$,
$$\inf_a E g_{N,m}(a-H)=E g_{N,m}(H-b),\qquad \lim_{N\to\infty}\lim_{m\to\infty}E g_{N,m}(H-b)=E L(H-b).$$
Each summand is symmetric and quasi-convex; no quasi-convexity of their sum is asserted.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume AC and a parametric model QMD at $\theta_0$ with score $s_{\theta_0}$.
Then
$$E_{\theta_0}s_{\theta_0}=0,$$
and the information matrix
$I_{\theta_0}=E_{\theta_0}[s_{\theta_0}s_{\theta_0}^T]$ has finite entries
and is positive semidefinite. The QMD convention and square-integrability of
the score are those of [[def-qmd-path]].

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume AC. Let $\{P_{n,h}:h\in\mathbb R^d\}$ be LAN at $h=0$ with
positive-definite information matrix $K$ and central sequence $\Delta_n$.
Let $T_n=\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_0)$ be regular under every fixed
local alternative, with common limit law $W$ as in
[[def-regular-estimator-under-local-alternatives]]. Then there is a
probability law $\nu$ on $\mathbb R^d$ such that
$$\mathcal L(W)=N_d(0,K^{-1})*\nu.$$
Here $*$ is convolution, the law of the sum of independent random vectors
with the two indicated laws. In particular, the efficient Gaussian component
with covariance $K^{-1}$ is a convolution factor of every regular limit.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[def-qmd-path]]. Write $p_0=p_{\theta_0}$,
$p_u=p_{\theta_0+u}$, and $P_0=P_{\theta_0}$. Let
$$\alpha(u):=P_{\theta_0+u}(p_0=0),\qquad \beta(u):=P_0(p_u=0).$$
Then $\alpha(u)=o(\|u\|_2^2)$ and $\beta(u)=o(\|u\|_2^2)$ as $u\to0$.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume AC and [[def-qmd-path]] at $\theta_0$ with score $s$ and information $I$.
Let $h_n\to h$ in $\mathbb R^d$, put $u_n=h_n/\sqrt n$, and write
$P_0=P_{\theta_0}$ and $P_{u_n}=P_{\theta_0+u_n}$. On
$S=\{p_{\theta_0}>0\}$ define, for all sufficiently large $n$,
$$q_n(x)=\frac{\mathbf1_S(x)p_{\theta_0+u_n}(x)} {(1-\alpha_n)p_{\theta_0}(x)},\qquad \alpha_n=P_{u_n}(S^c).$$
Then $q_n$ is a probability density relative to $P_0$. For IID
$X_1,\ldots,X_n\sim P_0$, let $L_n=\prod_{i=1}^nq_n(X_i)$ and
$\Delta_n=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^ns(X_i)$. Under $P_0^{\otimes n}$,
$$\log L_n=h_n^T\Delta_n-\tfrac12h^TIh+o_P(1),\qquad P_0^{\otimes n}(L_n=0)\to0.$$
Moreover, if $\bar P_n=q_nP_0$ is the normalized absolutely continuous
component of $P_{u_n}$ relative to $P_0$, then
$$\|P_{u_n}^{\otimes n}-\bar P_n^{\otimes n}\|_{\rm TV}\to0.$$
No full likelihood ratio for $P_{u_n}^{\otimes n}$ is asserted.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.before:
Assume AC. Let $\{P_{n,h}:h\in\mathbb R^d\}$ be a pointwise LAN experiment in the sense of [[def-lan-experiment]], with positive-definite information matrix $K$. Let $L:\mathbb R^d\to[0,M]$ be Borel measurable, symmetric and quasi-convex. Then
$$\liminf_{c\to\infty}\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat h_n}\sup_{\|h\|_2\le c}E_{P_{n,h}}L(\widehat h_n-h)\ge E L(Z),\qquad Z\sim N_d(0,K^{-1}).$$
The infimum includes every measurable randomized estimator. Only pointwise LAN at each fixed local parameter is required: no compact-uniform likelihood approximation, joint parameter likelihood field or posterior selector assumption is imposed.
changes.after:
Assume AC and let $d\ge1$ be finite. Let $\{P_{n,h}:h\in\mathbb R^d\}$ be a finite-dimensional
experiment that is LAN at $h=0$ with positive-definite information $K$ and
central sequence $\Delta_n\Rightarrow N_d(0,K)$ as in
[[def-lan-experiment]]. Let $M\ge0$ be finite and
$L:\mathbb R^d\to[0,M]$ be Borel measurable,
symmetric ($L(-x)=L(x)$), and quasi-convex (each sublevel set is convex).
Then
$$ \liminf_{c\to\infty}\liminf_{n\to\infty} \inf_{\widehat h_n}\sup_{\|h\|_2\le c} E_{P_{n,h}}L(\widehat h_n-h) \ge E L(Z),\qquad Z\sim N_d(0,K^{-1}). $$
The infimum ranges over measurable, possibly randomized estimators. The
experiment is pointwise LAN in each fixed $h$; no uniform likelihood-field
assumption is added.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\{P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\subseteq
\mathbb R^d\}$ be dominated by a common sigma-finite measure, with $\Theta$
open, and suppose the model is QMD at an interior $\theta_0$ with score $s$
and information $I=E_{\theta_0}[ss^T]$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID
$P_{\theta_0}$, and for each fixed local sequence $h_n\to h$ set
$u_n=h_n/\sqrt n$. Then the local product laws
$P_{\theta_0+u_n}^{\otimes n}$ admit mean-one likelihood-ratio proxies
$L_n$ relative to $P_{\theta_0}^{\otimes n}$ such that
$$\left\|P_{\theta_0+u_n}^{\otimes n}-L_nP_{\theta_0}^{\otimes n}\right\|_{\rm TV} \to0,$$
and under $P_{\theta_0}^{\otimes n}$,
$$\log L_n=h_n^T\Delta_n-\tfrac12h^TIh+o_P(1),\qquad \Delta_n=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^ns(X_i)\Rightarrow N_d(0,I).$$
Thus the IID QMD experiment is LAN in the proxy sense of
[[def-lan-experiment]]. This assertion does not claim that the full local
product law has a Radon–Nikodym derivative relative to the base law.

changes.before:
Let $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$ be measurable and suppose $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$
for every $x$. Then
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu.$$
changes.after:
Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. Let $f_n:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable for every $n\ge1$, with $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$, and suppose $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$ for every $x\in X$. Then
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

changes.heading: Definition
changes.after:
Let $\mathcal X$ be a set, let $\mathcal A$ be a sigma-algebra on it, let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, and let $\mu$ be a fixed sigma-finite measure on $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$. Suppose $(p_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ is a specified family of nonnegative measurable densities with $\int p_\theta\,d\mu=1$. Let $P$ be the actual data probability measure; it need not equal any model law $p_\theta\mu$ ([[def-probability-measure]]). Assume $p_\theta(X)>0$ $P$-almost surely and $\ell_\theta(X):=\log p_\theta(X)$ is integrable under $P$ for every parameter considered. Expectation means integration against $P$ ([[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]]).

The population log-likelihood criterion is $M_P(\theta):=\mathbb E_P[\ell_\theta(X)]$. A **pseudo-true parameter** is any maximizer $\theta^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\theta\in\Theta}M_P(\theta)$. It is unique when this argmax set is the singleton $\{\theta^*\}$. The model is **misspecified relative to $P$** when $P\ne p_\theta\mu$ for every $\theta\in\Theta$. This definition does not assert existence, uniqueness, interiority, or separation of the maximizer; those are theorem hypotheses when needed.

changes.heading: Statement
changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be IID from a probability law $P$ that is misspecified relative to the density family $p_\theta$, and let $\ell_\theta=\log p_\theta$ be as in [[def-pseudo-true-parameter-under-misspecification]]. Write $P_nf=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nf(X_i)$ and $M(\theta)=\mathbb E_P\ell_\theta(X)$. Assume that $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and that $\theta^*$ is the unique separated interior maximizer of $M$, where interior means that some Euclidean open ball about $\theta^*$ lies in $\Theta$: for each $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\eta_\varepsilon>0$ such that $M(\theta^*)-M(\theta)\ge\eta_\varepsilon$ whenever $\theta\in\Theta$ and $\|\theta-\theta^*\|_2\ge\varepsilon$.
